This complete cessation of movement is contrary to the principle of dynamics. In this universe nothing can stop moving: absolute pause or absolute speed simply do not exist. Pause and speed are relative. The cessation of movement is contrary to the principle of relativity, because between these two stages the relative factors are ever-active. It is these factors which cause one stage to be converted into a subsequent stage. This is how the flow of creation proceeds in matter, in mind and in consciousness. When movement reaches the point of maximum crudification, it is given a severe jolt by the relative factors. At that stage there is no scope for further crudification, because the nadir point of crudity has already been reached. This nadir point is called svayambhú. The jolt caused by the impact of the relative factors causes the flow of creation to move towards Consciousness, that same consciousness which was once converted into abstract. Consciousness, abstract and matter are the terms used to describe the same Entity in different forms, in three different stages. Some learned fools incorrectly interpret these three stages as being different entities, thereby creating confusion in the common people. These three stages can be likened to ice, water and vapour – the basic substance is the same it merely takes different forms.

此種行動的完全停止違反了動力原則。在此宇宙中，無一物可以停止運行。絕對的停止或絕對的速度是不存在的，停止和速度都是相對的。行動的停止違反相對世界的法則，因為在停止和速度之間的階段，相對因素永遠活躍不已。就是這些相對因素造成一個階段接著另一個階段出現。這也就是創造的波流何以在物質、心靈以及意識中不斷進行的原因。當行動到達最粗鈍的那一點時，相對因素會造成它劇烈的震動，表示此時就再也無法變得更粗鈍化了，因為已經到了粗鈍化的極致點了。這一點就稱為「創造的終點」(svayambhú)，因相對因素之衝擊所造成的震動使得創造的波流向意識前進│此同樣的意識曾一度被轉化為抽象的。宇宙意識、抽象的意識、具象的物質，都是用以描述在不同階段中、在不同形象中那個同樣的本體。有些愚蠢的大學者錯誤地將此三階段解釋成三個不同的實體，造成一般人的混淆。這三階段可比喻作冰、水和水蒸氣│是同一物的三態變化。

This crudest point, svayambhú, is an object of the Cognitive Faculty; the three stages are objects of the Cognitive Faculty and time, space and person functioning within these stages are also the objects of the Cognitive Faculty. The nature of time, space and person is such that when they work on a subtle level they automatically work in a subtle manner. In the subtlest stage, space is not like this terrestrial earth, time is not like the hands of a watch, and person is not like the human form as we know it. Rather in that stage the relative factors assume immense proportions: space is the vast spatial expression which even accommodates Consciousness. Time becomes capable of reckoning the Cosmic Mind, and person is none other than Saguńa Brahma. In a well-ordered environment of time, space and person, the finite objects maintain the closest link with Parama Puruśa. Once the mind is created, Parama Puruśa is reflected on the mind. That internal reflection is called guńátmá. That is, jiivátmá could reside in the five fundamental factors also if they had minds what to speak of matter. Even a living protozoa has a mind, although a very undeveloped one, so it too receives the reflection of the vast Cosmic Mind. Thus, whenever mind is expressed, or whenever the mind has originated but is not yet fully expressed, the Átman is reflected. Where there is no mind, the material body is directly guided by the Cosmic Mind; otherwise, it is guided by its own small unit mind. Whatever exists in this orderly world be it matter or mind-stuff, trees, plants, birds or animals, or human beings, reflects Parama Puruśa. Thus Parama Puruśa is the witness of everything – nothing can be kept secret from Him.

What is the unit mind? The Macrocosmic Mind originates from Macrocosmic Consciousness. Just as the five fundamental factors originate from the Macrocosmic Mind, similarly out of matter evolves the abstract. The unit is created due to clash and cohesion, which takes place within every material structure. This mind tries to take command of all the activities of that structure, thereby establishing its total authority. But the question is, where does the unit mind, which exists in a protozoa, an evolved human being or a learned scholar, actually come from? The unit mind is a metamorphosed form of matter, and matter is a metamorphosed form of Cosmic Mind. In the process of evolution, the Cosmic Mind takes the form of matter. 何謂「個體心靈」？大宇宙心靈從大宇宙意識中出現，正如同五大基本原素自大宇宙心靈中出現，抽象之物亦自物質中演化而來。個體心靈因摩擦和凝聚而被創造出來，此發生於每一個物質結構體中，此心靈意欲控制此結構體之所有一切活動以建立其完全的主導權。但問題是這個存在於單細胞生物、開展的人類或大學者的個體心靈到底從何而來？個體心靈是由物質演化而來，而物質是由大宇宙心靈演化而來。在演化的過程裡，大宇宙心靈取得物質的形象。和大宇宙心靈相較，個體心靈很明顯地非常小，何以能夠指望如此渺小的心靈用邏輯來分析或判斷至上意識呢？企圖如此做的人簡直是自大傲慢，這是白費時間的無益追尋。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

True human beings are those who move according to the natural impetus of time, space and person. They study their surroundings and the historical events which have caused the present, and the direction in which society should move in future. True human beings can discriminate between right and wrong, just and unjust. True human beings are sure that their goal is the Supreme Goal and they move towards it with steady untiring steps. Only when the true Goal is realized can we say that the auspicious dawn has come in life, and people are worthy to be called human beings. Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

The innate characteristic of the human mind is that it requires physical objects (ábhoga or physical pabulum) for the preservation of physical existence; subtle psychic objects (subtle pabulum) for satisfaction and expansion, and the greatest object of all, Parama Puruśa, the Supreme Goal of life (álambana or the Supreme Desideratum.) Physical objects are limited, for they exist within the periphery of time, space and person. Thus one day they will be totally exhausted. Something which is dear today will be despised tomorrow, and may be treated with indifference the day after tomorrow. An item of food which tastes delicious when it is fresh, may be totally unpalatable after a while. This is what usually happens in the mundane world.

人類心靈本自具有的特性即是它需要物質的標的(ábhoga或物質性食糧)來維持它身體的存在、需要精細的心智標的以滿足其心理的擴展、需要一切中最偉大的目標│至上意識│做為生命的至上目標(álambana)。物質之物極為有限，因為它們存在於時、空、人物的範疇中，所以終有一朝它們將被完全耗盡。某些在今日被視為親愛之物明日將被棄如敝屣，在後天更可能被視為行同陌路；在賞味期間覺得可口之極品菜餚，過期後也許難吃無比。世間之事通常如此。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

Suppose you are attending a party, and have a craving for more rasogollas but your stomach is so full that to eat another is a physical impossibility. You return home disappointed, for you think that had you eaten a few more you would have enjoyed the party even more. This is what happens with physical pabulum – being limited it cannot provide unending satisfaction. But the flow of subtle psychic pabulum is endless. Because of its limitlessness, the human mind cannot accept it endlessly. After enjoying it for a while one becomes tired. This sort of pabulum can never provide one with supreme satisfaction or supreme development either. Hence we cannot call psychic pabulum the desideratum of life.

假定你參加一個宴會，你很想再多吃些甜點(rasogollas)，但你的胃已經飽到連一個也塞不下了，你沮喪地回到家後心想：如果你能再多吃幾個，這個宴會將帶給你更大的滿足。這就是物質性食糧帶來的結果│它們非常有限，永遠不會帶來真正的滿足。然而精細的心智食糧之波流卻是無限的，但由於其無限，人類心靈又無法無止境地全盤接收它們，在享受過一陣子後人們開始覺得疲乏。這種食糧也永遠不可能帶來真正至上的滿足或無上的發展。因此心智食糧亦非生命之真正目標。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

Something which we cannot accept permanently we may call pabulum, but the desideratum of the spiritual world should not be called pabulum because there is no one to enjoy the pabulum. What deserves to be called the desideratum? The desideratum can only be that Entity which remains unassailed by the three relative factors. Therefore the only desideratum is Parama Puruśa, for He alone remains beyond the periphery of time, space and individuality. The three relative factors are born after the process of metamorphosis begins from Shambú Liuṋga. Parama Puruśa is the only Absolute Entity; everything else is relative. So if one wants to attain the highest realm of existence one will have to transcend the domain of relativity, for everything relative, undergoes metamorphosis.

某些我們無法永恆持有之物稱為「食糧」(pabulum)，但靈性世界的目標不應該被稱為「食糧」，因為在此沒有享受此一食糧的享受者存在。何者值得被稱為「目標」？唯有那不受上述三個相對因素影響的本體是我們的目標。因此，只有至上意識是吾人的目標，唯有祂能卓絕獨立於時、空、人物的影響外。相對因素產生於創造之起點(Shambú Liuṋga)開始後的演變過程。至上意識是絕對唯一的本體，其他都是相對產生的實體，故若想達到存在最高的境界，則吾人必須超越於相對的領域，因為在相對領域裡，萬事萬物恆處於無常變化之中。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

If the human mind has to accept something as its object, it should only accept Parama Puruśa, and nothing else. If it is to accept any entity without a second, then Parama Puruśa alone should be accepted. If any entity is to be known, then only Parama Puruśa should be accepted as the object of knowledge, and none else. Whatever is a desideratum is certainly a mental object. But the Cognitive Faculty is the subject, because He is witnessing everyone and everything. Whatever is being created is a different stage of creation. He is the subject and all other entities are His objects. He is the witnessing entity because He is the Supreme controller. Human beings are His object.
倘若人類心靈必須接受某物為其目標，它唯一應該接受的就只有至上意識了。如果它只能有一個實體為目標，則非至上意識莫屬。任何有待了悟的實體中，唯有至上意識應被做為了悟的目標。任何被選為目標的必然是一種心智的客體，然而至上認知能力是主體，因為祂見證萬有一切。任何被創造出來的東西都是在創造的不同階段中所出現的，而祂是主體，其他的所有一切都是祂的客體，祂是見證的實體，因為祂乃至上控制者，人類是祂的客體。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

Likewise when human beings accept Parama Puruśa as the polestar of their lives, then Parama Puruśa becomes the object and human beings become the subject. But how is that possible? When He is the Supreme Subject of all objectivities, then how can He be your object? He is the subject, you are His object. But at the same time no one except Parama Puruśa should be made the object of life. Nothing except the Supreme Entity is dependable – no one except Parama Puruśa deserves to be the goal of life. So what is the solution? Rationality proves that He is the subject of all objects; but on the other hand we find that only He should be made the object of life. But is that possible? Yes, it is.

同樣的，當人類以至上意識為其生命之指引時，人類變成主體，至上意識反而成為他的客體。但這怎麼可能呢？當祂是所有客體的至上主體時，祂又怎麼可能變成你的客體呢？祂是主體，你才是祂的客體，但同時你又不應選擇至上意識之外的任何實體做為你生命的目標，除了至上本體外你沒有任何可以依靠的了│除了至上意識外，沒有任何實體可以是你生命的目標。該如何是好？理性證明祂是所有客體的主體，而且除了祂以外我們再也找不到任何可以做為生命目標的實體，這怎麼可能呢？是的，這是可能的。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

Human beings work according to the divine plan and while working they take the name of the Lord. They ideate on Him and think internally, “ I am His object and He is my subject. He is seeing whatever I am doing.” So He remains the subject throughout. When He is made an object it is for the purpose of ideation on Him. His ever wakeful conscience will constantly warn me, “What are you doing? He is watching you.”

Now let us return to the interpretation of karma-sannayása (cardinal spirit of action). According to some interpretations, it means total inactivity. Now who is the doer of karma? We know that the range of action is limited within the arena of time, space and person. So there are two functional agents or doers of action: the microcosm on the one hand and the Macrocosm on the other. Apart from these two, no third entity can be of any relevance in the matter of attaining the proper finality of action. The awakening of psychic desire at any moment compels the physical body to be active, but the body is incapable of any function in the absence of an impetus from the mind. There are two reasons for this. First, there is always the attraction of the Cosmic Mind. Therefore if there is any command from the Supreme, the individual entity is bound to move. Secondly, the unit mind can direct the movement of any other entity in spite of its unwillingness. Hence an action is executed either by a unit mind or by the Cosmic Mind. The wind blows: wind is a blind force devoid of its own psyche. This wind is a material entity, but it moves due to the impetus from the Cosmic Mind. It is similar to that of a top spun by young boys. Boys cannot always spin the tops; they spin only when they are thrown in a particular way, in a perfect fashion, otherwise not. A top has no power to spin unless it is made to do so by a second entity. Likewise the sun is moving around its nucleus with its large family of celestial bodies under Divine inspiration. Hence all physical activities originate from the mind which is the prime mover of all actions. No action can take place without the impulse of mind.

誰是從事行動者？我們知道行動侷限在時、空、人物的範疇中，所以有兩個行動者：一個是個體小宇宙，另一個則是大宇宙心靈。除此二者，沒有第三個實體可以正確地在行動中達到其最後的目標。心智渴望的覺醒隨時驅策著身體從事行動，但是身體若無來自心靈的動力則根本無法作用。對於這點，它有兩個理由—第一，大宇宙心靈的吸引是永遠存在的，因此任何來自至上的命令，個體就一定要行動。第二，不論願意與否，個體心靈可以引導任何其他實體的運作。因此，行動是由個體心靈或大宇宙心靈所執行。風吹，風是沒有自己心智的盲目力量。它是一個物質實體，依據大宇宙心靈的驅策而行動。就像是小孩子在玩陀螺，只有以特別的方法、技巧投擲時它才會旋轉，否則它就無法旋轉。所以陀螺除非經由第二個實體的作用，否則它是沒有力量旋轉的。同樣的，太陽隨同其銀河系的大家庭在至上的激勵下環繞其核心運轉。因此，所有物質上的行動源自心靈，心靈是一切行動最初的運作者。沒有心靈的驅策就不會有行動。

Both the unit mind and the Cosmic Mind function within the bounds of time, space and person, but the difference between the two is that the unit mind may not necessarily consciously comprehend the function of Cosmic Mind, although it (the unit) comprehends on its unconscious level. And even what remains unknown to the unit mind is certainly known to the Supreme, because the Cosmic Mind maintains this cognizant bearing with its independent will. The function of the Cosmic Mind may or may not be prompted by any causes. Regarding the Macrocosmic function, it may be said that it may or may not take place within the relative factors of time, space and person. As long as the causal stance of the microcosmic function of Parama Puruśa remains within the scope of time, space and person, the unit may be graced with that very realization. Now let us analyse how the mind functions. In the physical sphere energy is essential for action. What is energy? Energy is the actional state within a material structure. This energy by itself is a blind force and for its activation intellect must exist: a driver is required to direct this blind force. The support of the intellect is a prime necessity for the operation of energy in this material world. 1. 【拒絕無意義死音譯】：如 Praṇipāta, Pariprashna, Sādhana, Dharma 等專名，直接保留標準羅馬拼音梵字。
2. 【正名昇華】：
   - 將 Tantra 譯為『搪碴』(取掃除粗鈍之意) 或保留原文，絕不可使用容易混淆的『密宗』。
   - 將 Surrender 譯為『誠服』(真誠信賴託付)，絕不可使用帶有封建階級壓迫的『臣服』。
   - 將 Sevá 譯為『服務』、『服務眾生』，或雅稱『協峇』(取台語峇 va 音，協和奉獻)。
3. 文風典雅莊重，純淨正體中文，具備微言大義的靈性美感。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

Undeveloped human beings consider themselves to be very intelligent and thus at every step they invite innumerable obstacles in the material world. Later on, after climbing some rungs up the ladder of evolution, they realize form the core of their hearts the hollowness of their psychic capabilities. It is the natural rule of the universe that those who possess immense knowledge are quite conscious of their intellectual limitations, whereas people with superficial knowledge think just the opposite. The genuine way of learning for seekers of knowledge is to consider always that they know nothing.
心智未開展的人，自以為聰明，在世俗世界每一階段都會遇到無數的挫折和阻礙。之後在進化的道上向前邁進了幾步，他們內心深處深切的了解心智的力量是如此的空虛。學富五車知識淵博的人，方才完全了解他們聰明才智的有限，而知識淺薄的人其想法正好相反，這是宇宙自然的法則。求知的人最純正的學習方法，就是永遠認為他們什麼都不知道。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

Now what is the method to merge the unit mind in the Cosmic Mind? As the basic trend of the evolutionary process is from the crude towards the subtle, therefore in order to make oneʼs own intellect subtle, one is to take the ideation of the subtlest entity, not to remain engrossed in crude objects. With the constant ideation of the Supreme, the mind will gradually attain more and more subtlety and will ultimately be converted into the subtlest entity. After this the sense of separation in the microcosm ceases to exist, and it becomes one with the Cosmic Mind. When the unit intellect arrives at this highest point, there is no doubt that it has become one with the Supreme Intellect. This state of pinnacled intellect is called karma-sannyása. So wise people should be ever vigilant regarding karma-sannyása.
如何將個體心靈融入大宇宙心靈？如果進化的過程是從粗鈍走向精細，為了使我們的聰明才智也精細化，吾人必須以最精細的實體為理念導向，而不是熱衷於粗鈍的事物。藉著心念不斷觀想、持念至上意識，心靈會逐漸精細，最後就會轉變成最精細的實體。當小宇宙個體的這種分離感不再存在時，它就與大宇宙心靈合而為一。

What is knowledge? Knowledge is the subjectivisation of external objectivities. When external objectivities are not subjectivised, there occurs either internal or external reflection or refraction on the mental plate. This is nothing but the resultant of external or internal projections. This is not true knowledge, or direct knowledge; in fact, it is not knowledge at all but a shadow of knowledge. Those who only reach up to the range of reflection or refraction develop ego. But those who are truly learned are devoid of any ego, because they are well aware of the subjective cause of all external objectivities.

To understand the meaning of pará-bhakti, it is essential to know its supreme aim, because pará-bhakti is closely related to karma sannyása. Every action has its end, its objective. The movement towards such an objective has two trends which are known as átmanepadii and parasmaepadii. If a person is greatly attracted towards a limited object, his or her mind will rush towards that object, and when at last the mind attains it, it gradually becomes one with that object. At that time, action and knowledge vanish for they take the form of that object.
了解至上虔誠的意義，是了解它最高的目標所不可或缺的，因為至上的虔誠與行動的基本精神有密切的關係。每個行動有其終點，有其目標。朝向這種目標的活動有兩個趨向：一者為被動(átmanepadii)形態，一者為主動(parasmaepadii)形態。如果人受有限之物的吸引，他們的心靈就會奔向那個物體，得到它時，其心靈會逐漸與彼物合一。那時，行動和知識因已與所追求之物合一而消失了。

You may have noticed, for example, that when some learned people earn recognition or a high degree, they lose interest in even discussing the subject of their degree. Can a human brain, with the help of a few nerve cells within a little cranium, with the faint flickers of the intellect, and by following the path of logic, attain the Supreme? Araneśu. Arańi means firewood, fuel.Fire lies hidden in firewood. To produce fire you have to rub two pieces of wood together to create friction. Similarly the Supreme Cognitive Faculty lies covert in you. If you create friction in your mind by adhering to truth and performing penance, the fire of meditation will ignite within. This will make it easier for you to realize the dormant Cognitive Faculty.Parama Puruśa or the Supreme Entity can only be realized through truth and penance, and when one has a one-pointed desire to realize Him. There is no other way. Without exclusive devotion to Parama Puruśa nothing can be attained. Mere philosophical knowledge will not help one to attain Him. A person may become a doctorate in twenty subjects, but that will not help him attain the Supreme. To attain Him one must cultivate one-pointed devotion for Him. Hence the most pedantic scholar may fail completely in attaining the Supreme Entity, whereas the most illiterate person may succeed. Parama Puruśa is not bothered about who is a great scholar or who is illiterate. He only considers the degree of oneʼs mental elevation. Thus the only way to attain Parama Puruśa is to develop an exclusive devotion for Him by embracing a life of truth and regular penance. Those who try to know the Supreme Entity with their intellect may at best gain a superficial knowledge of Him – superficial because the mind can never reach Him. If the mind cannot reach Him how can the human intellect explain what He is.

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

Parama Puruśa cannot do two things. He cannot create another Parama Puruśa like him. He is always One without a partner. He is One and He will remain One forever. Deva is always One. Here Deva means the expression of the Supreme Occult Power. This expression is the hub of the cosmological order. All other expressions of the divine power have emanated from the Supreme Entity, Parama Shiva. We can easily perceive those individual divine vibrations because they come within the scope of our sense organs. But we can only perceive them partially, not fully. For example, we can only perceive a light wave within a certain range of wavelengths. If the wavelength of the light is beyond that range perception is impossible. That is why we cannot see an object in dim light, even though there is some light. And that is why our eyes are blinded by a strong light. Thus the eyes only have the capacity to function within a limited range. The same principle applies to sound waves. Our auditory organs cannot hear a soft sound and are deafened when a sound is too loud. Our sense organs function within the medium range of wavelengths.

至上意識有兩件事祂做不到：一是祂無法創造另一個和祂一模一樣的至上意識，祂永遠是獨一無二的存在，永遠是唯一的。神(Deva)只有唯一的那一個，在此「神」意指至上法力的展現。此種展現是宇宙秩序的核心，所有其他神聖力量的展現皆源自於至上本體(Parama Shiva)。我們可以很容易感知到那些各別的神聖波流，因為它們在我們感知的範疇裡，但我們只能感知部分，不能感知全體。比方說，我們只能看到某波長範圍內的光波，在這些範圍外的光波我們即無法接收得到，所以在昏暗之下我們看不到物體的樣貌，即使在微弱的燈光下我們也很難看清楚。同樣的，在強烈的光線下我們的眼睛也是如同目盲般看不見。因此，眼睛只能作用在有限的範圍內。聲音亦同，我們的聽覺器官聽不見極細微的聲音，而大音希聲，過於大聲我們同樣也是聽不見的。我們的感官都只能在某一特定波長的範疇內運作。

Eko Devah. This Deva, that is Parama Deva or Parama Shiva, is the Supreme Source of all partial physical, psychic and spiritual emanations. He is the nucleus of the entire cosmos. Therefore, He is described as Eko Deva, the One Deva. The question arises, when the mind cannot reach Him, how can we justify using a numeral, which is a finite term, to describe Him? Numerals such as one, two, three, four, five, etc. are merely psychic concepts. So how can a numeral be used when the mind is unable to comprehend Him? Eka or one is a numeral Similarly aneka (many) is also a numeral. Now the reason why He can be described as Eka or One is that it is only when the mind becomes pinnacled or one pointed that a person can become one with Him.

Eko Devah：「此唯一之神」，意即「至上之神」，祂是身、心、靈所有各局部分支展現的至上來源，祂是全宇宙之核心。因此，祂被形容成「唯一之神」(Eko Deva)。問題是如果心靈無法達到祂，那麼我們何以能夠使用一個有限的數字來描述祂呢？一、二、三、四、五等等數字只是一種心智上的概念，所以如果連心靈都無法知曉祂，我們又怎能用數字去表示祂呢？一(Eka)是一個數目字，相同的，「許多」(aneka)也是一個數目字，以「一」來描述祂是因為唯有當心靈達到最高點或專心集中於一點時，吾人方能與祂合而為一。

The question is, how can one acquire such spiritual force? By sincerity, one can acquire psychic force, and through the practice ofsádhaná[spiritual practice] one can acquire spiritual force. Those who are persistent in their endeavour do acquire psychic force. When one sits down to meditate after attaining that sort of psychic energy one easily acquires spiritual force. That spiritual force lies latent in you; it is not difficult to attain. You should ensure that the path ofsádhanáyou choose is not a defective one in which there is a mistake in the beginning, middle, and end. One should move ahead in oneʼs mission after determining oneʼs goal. Once the goal is fixed there remains almost no possibility, of error; hence you should always remember your goal. But once you fall into the trap of error it leads to danger. This is the reason why I advise people to remember theirguru mantra, to always remain aware of the goal. The souls of those people who practicesádhanáin this way enter the abode ofBrahma. Persistent endeavour and practical cult are essential to reach the goal. Hence insádhanáone should remember two essential factors: constant awareness of oneʼs goal, and persistent endeavour to attain that goal.

There is a subtle difference betweenliiláandkriid́á. When the cause of an effect is easily discernible it is calledkriid́a, but when the cause is unknown and only the effect is easily discernible it is calledliilá. This creation is theliiláofParama Puruśabecause human beings do not know why He has created it. With the help of their intellect they are eager to know the cause of creation, but will they ever be successful in this quest? They want to solve the riddle of creation, but they have no notion about the cause. So whateverParama Puruśadoes is all Hisliilá, It cannot be called Hiskriid́á. I have already said that when one discovers the relation between the cause and effect it is calledkriid́á, but when one can see only the effect and not the cause, it is calledliilá. For human beings having only a small unit mind the creation is the liilá ofParama Puruśa, but to Him it is His kriid́á. For instance, in the relative world wherever there is time, space, and person, and wherever the limited intellect can function, we can discover the cause behind every action. In this connection you remember the oft-quoted aphorism of Maharśi Kańada:Kárańábhávat káryábháva– “Where there is no cause there is no effect.” In the process of tracing the cause-effect relationship back to its original cause we arrive at the last stage. Beyond this stage action does not remain within the scope of time, space and person. Since the cause remains beyond the scope of the three relative factors, it does not also come within the periphery of mind. If the mind transcends the periphery of the relative factors it is automatically annihilated.

Jiṋátvá shivaḿ shántimatyantameti.Parama Puruśais Shiva. By knowing Him human beings can attain absolute peace. What we callShaktiin ordinary terms isPrakrti. SoParama PuruśaisCitishakti, andPrakrtiis His immanent power. Only ifCitishaktipermits it, can the binding faculty ofPrakrtiinfluence Him. But if the Cognitive Faculty does not desire it, the Operative Force ofPrakrtiis helpless. Then Shiva remains dormant in His unmanifested stance. We witness the manifested state when the Cognitive Faculty permits the Operative Force to operate. So when someone attains freedom from bondage it means he or she is freed from the bondage of the Operative Principle, and is thus established in the Cognitive Faculty. Jiṋátvá shivaḿ shántimatyantameti：至上意識即宇宙意識│希瓦(Shiva)。了悟祂則可獲得絕對永恆的平靜。Shánti這個字是源自梵文動詞字根sham加上字尾ktin。Shánti意指融入於自己的自性當中。一個人可藉由了悟祂而得到心靈的平靜，這就是我們說的shánti。至上意識被稱為宇宙意識(Shiva)，宇宙意識就是至上認知能力(Citishakti)，亦即宇宙意識也是某種的力量(Shakti)。一般我們所稱的宇宙力量指的是造化勢能(Prakrti)，所以至上意識是至上認知能力，而造化勢能是祂所具有的執行力量。只有在至上認知能力的允諾下，造化勢能的束縛力量才能作用於祂；如果至上認知能力不想如此，造化勢能是完全無法運作的。故宇宙意識蟄伏在其自身未展現的境界，我們只能看見至上認知能力允許造化勢能運作所展現的那個部分。所以，當某人從束縛中獲得解脫，則意指此人從運作法則的束縛中獲得解脫，而將自身立足於至上認知能力的境界中。故而有言道：了悟至上意識則可獲得絕對永恆的平靜(Jiṋátvá shivaḿ shántimatyantameti)。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

There are some other people who exhort others by saying, “Success in human life lies in God-realization, and you should do ásanas and práńáyáma and other practices. When your mind and its psychic propensities will be completely suspended, you will realize Parama Puruśa.”This is called hat́ha yoga. Ha is the acoustic root of sun or fire, and t́ha is the acoustic root of moon or calmness. Now when these two opposing flows, ha and t́ha–one is the actional flow, and the other is the cessation of the actional flow, the idá and the piuṋgalá–are forcibly made to become one, this is called hat́ha yoga. Thus when something which was not expected is done suddenly or forcibly, we use the expression hat́hát.

也有些人勸他人說道：「人類生命的成就就在於了悟至上，所以，你應該從事瑜伽體位法和呼吸控制法等的鍛鍊。當你的心靈和心靈習性完全停止作用時，你將會了悟至上意識。」此稱為「哈達瑜伽」(hat́ha yoga)。Ha是太陽或火的音根，而t́ha是月亮或平靜的音根。當這兩種相反的波流(ha和t́ha)──一個是行動的波流，一個是停止行動的波流；一個左脈(idá)和一個右脈(piuṋgalá)──被強行合併時，就稱為「哈達瑜伽」。所以，當某些事在意料之外突然或強行被迫發生時，我們就會使用「哈達」(hat́hát)來表示。

So there are two meaning for the word iśt́a: first, the one whose realization fills the mind, thus removing all psychic dissatisfactions; and secondly, the most beloved of all entities. If Parama Puruśa wants to give you something you should say, “Oh Lord, many thanks, but I want nothing from you. If you really want to give me something, give Yourself to me. I do not want to fill my mind with mundane objects.” Thus Parama Puruśa alone is the iśt́a; and where there is dharma there is iśt́a and where there is iśt́a there is dharma. So dharma and iśt́a can never remain separate. Water and fish cannot exist separately; if fish are forcibly separated from water they will die. Likewise, Iśt́a also cannot be separated from dharma; and thus no one can proclaim that such-and-such dharma is atheistic because it does not accept the existence of the Supreme Entity. If one accepts dharma it means that one has accepted Iśt́a, and if one accepts Iśt́a it means that one has accepted dharma. Some people hypocritically assert that Mr. So-and-so does not believe in dharma. This is only an external show; internally he accepts dharma and thus he accepts Iśt́a also. It is sheer duplicity to speak thus, which is unbecoming and degrading for human beings.

Falsehood is the noumenal cause of all phenomenal crimes. Those who lie are hypocrites and cheats. All crimes and sins are embedded in falsehood. If a thief stops telling lies, then will any theft be possible? No, certainly not. According to the wise people, a thief must be free from two defects – but I want to add one more: 1) a thief should not stay awake during the day – a thief should sleep during the day and stay awake at night. 2) A thief must not speak the truth. If they constantly ideate on Him, if they always sing His glories and become engrossed in His ideation then they no longer remain ordinary mortals. Then they will achieve success in whatever task they undertake. But that success, that victory does not belong to them – it belongs to dharma, to Iśt́a.If the most powerful emperor of this sea-girt earth dares to fight against dharma, even a handful of gold in his hands will turn to a handful of dust, and he will meet with miserable defeat. This is the inexorable law of dharma. Thus I have said, “Where there is dharma there is Iśt́a, and where there is Iśt́a there is victory” You should always bear in mind that victory does not mean the victory of weak human beings – it means the victory of dharma, the victory of Iśt́a. Intelligent people who move firmly along the path of dharma and sit on the lap of Iśt́a are destined to be victorious. Todayʼs discourse however is about Parama Puruśa, not about Jiivátmá or Jiivapuruśa. External activity is the actual expression of whatever you think on your psychic plane. So, whatever your mind is acquainted with, is done by your mind and hence your Átmá comes to know it. To what extent does your Átmá maintain its witnessing capability? Whatever action the Cosmic Mind does, that is not really action because everything is internal. But whatever the unit mind performs is both internal as well as external. Sádhaná, therefore, is to unify the two into one – the internal “I” and the external “I”. Two-ness in one single personality is a disease. The more the gap between these two “Iʼs”, the more you will undergo psychic torment. You must remember that in this second half of the 20th Century people are feeling much gap in between their internal “I” and external “I”. Because of the trouble in adjusting these two “Iʼs” there is an increase in mental illnesses. This is the greatest disease in the 20th century. Two birds with beautiful plumage are seated on the same tree. One of them is tasting the sweet fruits of the tree, whereas the other is just looking on. They say that wherever there is action there is equal and opposite reaction. But there is one thing to be borne in mind here. Where there is action, the equal and opposite reaction takes place only when personal, temporal and spatial factors remain unchanged. But you know that personal, temporal and spatial factors do not remain unchanged. Just in the next moment time-factor is changed. If it is an inanimate object there is entitative change therein. If there is an animate object, the person remains unchanged but the mentality changes. Therefore, we do not find the exactly equal and opposite reaction of the action done. Had the time, space and person remain unchanged the reaction would also have been the same. So get it in mind, while doing some thing immoral be prepared to pay the interest too. It is better not to take a loan, then alone you will not have to pay the interest.

人們說有行為就必有相對應的反作用力行為。但在此處有一件事必須牢記於心，就是當作用力產生時，只有在時間、空間、人物因素都不變的情況下所產生的反作用力行為才會是相等的。而你知道時、空、人物因素不會保持不變，僅僅只是下一刻，時間因素就不同了。如果它是無生命的個體，那麼它的改變發生在個體內部；如果是有生命的個體，雖然他這個人沒有改變，但他的心理狀態可能已經改變了，因此，果報不可能與行為完全相等。通常果報會增強而非減弱，因為行為完成後的反作用力會使得心靈質內部的間隙更為增加。例如，若你借了一千塊盧比，當你歸還時，必須也要附上利息，可能總共必須歸還一千兩百塊或一千三百塊盧比。如果你犯了罪，你必須接受更多的懲罰的果報。倘若時、空、人物等因素維持不變，果報應該是相同的。所以你心中必須牢記，當你在做不道德之事時，你心中要有準備會付出利息。最好不要借貸，只有這樣才不需要付利息。

“Bhavakendra.” This external world, this expressed world, which you see is full of action, full of rhythms. This actional world is both extroversial and introversial for you. There is a world inside your mind. That is your internal world, and the world which you see without is the extroversial world. Hence this internal world for you is ideational and the external world, actional. But for Parama Puruśa there is nothing like the extroversial world, all is introversial, and hence for Him this world is ideational or His thought projection, i.e., this world is Samkalpita for Him. Suppose you imagine Jodhpur in your mind. This is ideational. But when you see outside, you find that it is Jaipur, not Jodhpur.(1)Then you realize that Jodhpur of your mind is ideational and Jaipur is actual. The same thing occurs in dream. While you dream you think it to be a fact because the external world does not exist there. For Parama Puruśa there is nothing like the extroversial world; just as for you when the internal world, which you take to be true in dream, is actually not there. For Him, the world exists in His ideation i.e., nothing is extroversial, rather all is introversial. And His imagination is called Samkalpa. Hence this world is a Samkalpita world for Him. There is a difference between Kalpatia and Samkalpana. Whatever you do in Kalpana is transitory and the Java concerned is only its enjoyer and none else.

「Bhavakendra」(至上理念波流的核心)：你所看見的這個外在世界，此一化現世界充滿了行動、韻律。這行動的世界對你而言既是向外的，也是向內的。你的心中有一個世界，那就是你的內在世界，而你於外面所看見的世界則是外在世界。因此，這個內在世界對你來說是想像的世界，而外在世界則是行動的世界。可是對至上意識而言，沒有所謂的「外在世界」，一切都是內在的。因此，對祂來說，此一世界是祂想像中的世界或者可說是祂思想的投射，亦即此一世界對祂而言，是祂的想像波流(Samkalpita)。假定你於心中想像鳩德埔，這是你的想像作用，而當你看到外面時，你發現那是齋義埔不是鳩德埔，於是你了解到你心中的鳩德埔原來是想像的，而是齋義埔才是真實的存在。同樣的事也發生在作夢時，當你作夢時，你以為它是真實的，因為此時外在世界並不存在。對至上意識來說，沒有外在世界這一回事，就好像你在作夢時把其實並不存在的內在世界當成是真實的一樣。對祂而言，這世界存在於祂的想像中，也就是說這所有一切都不是外在的，而是內在的，祂的想像力稱為「Samkalpa」，所以這世界對祂來說是祂的想像的波流。Kalpatia(想像)和Samkalpana(決意)是有區別的。任何你在想像中所做的都是短暫、無常的，而個體所關心的僅僅只是享樂，別無其他。

This world is ideational for Him and this ideational cosmos has Him in its centre. He is in the centre of this ideational cosmos. He has to control it. Have you ever seen a fisherman spreading his fishing net in a river or a tank? The fisherman does so and he has to manage the net also. Likewise, He has made the ideational world which He alone has to manage and control. He controls the idea, therefore, in common parlance, He is taken as inactive. If, however, people steal, rob and are corrupt, will Paramátmá say that He is Akartá and hence He has got nothing to do with them? No, He controls them indirectly through the Guńas. Actually He controls the Guńas which do the actions. Really it is Paramá-Prakrti that operates. For instance, the commander orders the soldiers to catch so and so. Who catches? It is the soldiers, the power of the soldiers. People see that the soldier has caught the offender, but the soldier does so only with the direction of his commander. Hence Parama Puruśa is just like the commander and Parama Prakrti just like the soldier. This control over Bhavakendra is Samkalpita Niyantrańa, and He who controls it is named Krśńa. Therefore, there is another name of Parama Puruśa i.e. Krśńa. Krsna means the attractor of this ideational world. This ideational world is made of ectoplasmic stuff or by ectoplasmic structure. For Parama Puruśa, the quinquelemental world is just the crudified form of His ectoplasm. His mental stuff is subtler than jiivas, and therefore contains speed (Gati), light (Dyuti) and rhythm (Chanda), and controls them. The mental stuff of Parama Puruśa with which the world has been created is something blissful (Svarasa). This very object is named Paramarasa. The unit mind does all with its mental stuff. Sometimes it creates money in the mind and seeing the mental bank balance it feels happy. Sometimes it makes itself a Prime Minister and feels happy, and sometimes it feels enemies are mentally beaten and it is overjoyed. All these are done only with an aim to satisfy its mental hunger, to quench its mental thirst. Ultimately we see that an individualʼs mental stuff is transformed into worldly objects. For the unit mind, whatever it makes within itself is Vaesayika. It is all directed for personal pleasure, for material pleasure. The flow of the ectoplasmic stuff of the jiiva is called Viśayarasa and the flow of Cosmic Mind is Paramarasa. When, even for once, the unit mind happens to come in contact with Paramarasa, the material pleasure ( viśayrasa) seems dry and insipid. Just as one eating vegetables without salt, feels they are tasteless. But material objects are needed to maintain the physical existence. The wise make the flow of Viśayarasa parallel to the flow of Paramarasa. They convert the waves of viśayarasa into the waves of Paramarasa. This alone is a safe way.

這個世界是祂的想像，而此一想像宇宙以祂為核心。祂是此想像宇宙的中心。祂必須控制這世界。你們看過漁夫在河流或水庫中撒網捕魚嗎？漁夫撒網也必須控制這個網。同樣的，祂創造了這個想像的世界，祂也必須管理和控制。祂控制著想像的波流，因此，用一般的說法，即祂被視為無行為者。如果人們偷竊、搶劫而且腐敗，至上意識可以說因為祂是無行為者就棄之不管嗎？不會的。祂會透過束縛的力量間接控制他們。事實上祂控制著這些從事行為的束縛力量。其實真正的運作者是造化力量。比方說，指揮官命令下屬士兵去逮捕某某某，從事逮捕工作的是誰？是士兵。人們看見士兵逮逮捕了罪犯，然而士兵之所以這麼做是因為長官的命令使然。因此，至上意識好比指揮官，而造化力量則如士兵。控制此想像波流的核心者就是「Samkalpita Niyantrańa」，這個控制者的名字就是克里斯那(Krśńa)，故至上意識又稱為克里斯那，克里斯那(Krśńa)意為「此想像世界的吸引者」。這個想像的世界是由心靈質創造出來的。對至上意識而言，五大原素世界是祂心靈質粗鈍化的結果。祂的心智構造比個體生命還要精細，因此包含並控制了速度(Gati)、光(Dyuti)和節奏(Chanda)。至上意識用以創造這個世界的心靈質是某種悅性之物(Svarasa)，稱之為「至上神性波流」(Paramarasa)。而個體心靈也用他們的心靈質做出一切，有時候他們在心中創造金錢，看見心中的銀行存款結餘而感到高興；有時候他會在心中創造自己是總理而感到高興，而有時候他會在心中打敗敵人而樂極忘形。所有這些都只為了滿足心靈的飢渴、填補心中的慾望。最後我們將發現到個體心靈質變成那個世俗之物。對個體心靈而言，任何心中所創造之物稱為Vaesayik。它全部導向於個人的享樂，都是為了物質的快樂。故個體心靈質的波流稱為「物質享樂波流」(Viśayarasa)，而大宇宙心靈波流則稱為「至上神性波流」(Paramarasa)。個體心靈只要一度曾經觸及此至上神性波流，就會覺得物質的享樂非常枯燥無味，好像在吃沒有鹽巴調味的蔬菜般淡而無味。然而物質之物是維持肉身存在之所需。故明智者會調整物質享樂的波流與至上神性波流一致，他們會將物質享樂的波流轉化為至上神性的波流，唯有這樣才是安全的道路。

Krśńa is the nucleus of the Paramarasa of Bháva Samudra and the unit minds are like boats in that MaháSamudra. As per the rise and fall of Paramarasa of Parama Puruśa, the unit minds are to rise and fall i.e. as boats rise and fall with the waves of the ocean. The unit mind intentionally or unintentionally has to dance according to the rhythms and waves created by Parama Puruśa. This they are bound to do, there is no escape. Even if someone says that he will not dance because he is ashamed of dancing, really he dances, anyway; he simply does not know it. Everybody dances in the Paramarasa-Samudra. The Viśayarasatmaka Jiiva has to dance. There is no way out, they are made to dance. This very thing is the Rasa Liilá of Krśńa. There is difference between Liilá and Kriidá. Kriidá is causal. Everything in this world of relativity is causal. But Parama Puruśa is beyond the scope of relativity. Why is He making the world dance? Why has He made Paramarasa-Samudra? The answer to this cannot be known in the world of causality. Why Paramátmá has done something has no answer because He is beyond the scope of causality. Hence that which is non-causal, that which is beyond the scope of causality is Liilá. Whatever Paramátmá does is Liilá, but what Jiiva does is Kriidá. The wise will do Kriidá in such a way as to adjust their waves with the waves of Liilá. They will not try to know why Liilámaya has done an action. They will simply try to know Liilámaya Himself. If you cannot know the cause of a trifling thing like dancing, how can you know the cause of the action of Liilámaya? Jiiva has a very small brain and a very small cranium. It is not possible for it to know the action of Liilámaya. Suppose someone is an MA in 20 subjects. If he or she is asked suddenly to appear in the MA examination, he will not pass – he will have to read again, then he will have to appear. This proves that the Jiiva fails even to succeed in its own Kriidá. So how can it understand the cause of the Liilá of Liilámaya? It cannot. The best approach is to love Him, is to join His party. If there is true love the Master Magician will certainly make you understand everything because the more the members of His party know, the more convenient it is for Him. Hence He is “Bhavakendrasthitah.”

克里斯那是至上理念波流之洋的核心，個體心靈就好比航行在該浩瀚海洋的船隻，隨著至上意識神性波流的起伏，個體心靈也跟著起伏，亦即船隻會隨著海洋的波浪而起伏。個體心靈有意無意都必須隨著至上意識所創造的波流韻律而舞，他們必須如此，不得不如此。即使有人說他不會跳所以不要跳，但他還是跳著舞，只是他自己不知道。每個人都在至上神性波流的海洋中舞動著。喜好物質享樂的個體生命必須舞動，他們沒有別的選擇，必須舞動。這就是克里斯那神性波流的遊戲(Liilá)。無緣由的神性遊戲和有緣由的遊戲(Kriidá)是不同的。Kriidá是具有原因的，在這相對世界中的每件事物都是有因果關係的，都能追溯它的原因。可是至上意識卻是超越於相對的世界。為什麼祂要讓這世界舞動呢？為什麼祂要創造這個神性波流的大海洋呢？這在因果世界是找不出答案的，為什麼至上意識做一些沒有解答的事呢？因為祂超越因果的範疇。因此，沒有原因，並且超越此因果範疇的，就稱為「神性遊戲」。至上意識所做一切都是「至上的神性遊戲」，而個體的所做所為都是有因果的。因此，明智的人，會調整他們在因果世界行為的波流與至上神性的波流一致。他們不會試圖想要去知道為什麼神性遊戲的幻化力量(Liilámaya)要這麼做，而只想要了悟此一宇宙力量本身。要是你連為什麼要舞動這樣的小事你都不懂，你又如何能得知為什麼宇宙幻化力量要這麼做呢？個體只有一個小小的腦袋和頭顱。他不可能會知道宇宙幻化力量的作為。假定有人有二十門學科的碩士學位，若他突然被要求參加這些學科的學位考試，他必然不會通過，他必須得重讀才可以再接受考試。此證明個體連自己已知之事都會失敗，又如何能夠去知曉宇宙幻化力量神性遊戲的原因呢？他是做不到的，最佳的辦法就是去愛祂，去加入祂，成為祂的一份子。如果與魔術大師間有真愛聯繫，祂當然會讓你知道所有的奧秘，因為越多祂的成員知道祂的奧秘，對祂來說就越方便。因此，我們說祂位於「俱屬性至上意識的核心」(Bhavakendrasthitah)。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

There is a particular tune, a particular rhythm, a particular rága, a particular rágini, particular laya and a particular tála in the Paramarasa-samudra as per the vibration projected in the nucleus of the Paramarasa. One who gets one acquainted with these does not like visayarasa, and naturally leaving the Visayarasa, one goes into Paramarasa.Then the attachment with the rága and rágini of Visayarasa is lessened and one becomes like a lunatic. People say correctly that Rádha, hearing the melodious tune of the flute of Krśńa, started behaving abnormally. The third one is to try to convert the psychic stuff into cognition. This effort is called the dharma. Dharma is of two types – primary and secondary. Then the fourth one is Samyak Ájiiva, proper physical and psychic occupation. One may earn money by stealing but it is not called a proper occupation. One may earn money by gambling but it is also not a proper occupation. Oneʼs occupation should be pure. It must not go against the interest of the collective body. Human beings are social creatures. Then, Smara nityamanityatám. Nityam means “always” – “Remember always the transitory nature of things.” [Anityatám means “the ephemeral”, “the transitory”.] That which was in the past, is in the present and will continue to be in the future is nitya. If even one of these three aspects of time be absent, the thing is not nitya. Niiti has a very close association with dharma. What is dharma? That which sustains the jiiva is dharma. And the practical side of dharma is expressed in the words Ácárańát dharmah, that is, “Dharma is the assemblage of all your conduct” – the way you eat, the way you speak, the way you perform sádhaná. If your conduct is good, dharma is with you; if your conduct is not good, dharma is not with you. And if dharma is not with you, what comes about is your sarvanásha, or sarvátmaka vinásha – that is, your physical, mental, and spiritual ruin. Now you may say that your átman cannot be ruined. That is correct, but your átman will not remain in the form of átman. It will become crudified.

導向靈性進步的行為和法性有著密切的關係。何謂「法性」？維持個體生命的就是法性。其實際的表現在於Ácárańát dharmah這個詞上，它的意思是「法性是你所有行為的集合」──你吃東西的方式、你說話的方式、你從事靈性修持的方式等。如果你的行為是好的，法性即與你同在； 如果你的行為是不好的，法性就不與你同行。如果法性不與你同行，就會導致滅絕的後果(sarvanásha或sarvátmaka vinásha)，亦即導致你身、心、靈全面的滅絕。或許你會說靈魂是永遠不滅的，這話誠然沒錯，但你的靈魂不會維持原本靈魂的形態，它會變得粗鈍化。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

In the first stage of dharma, the greatest helping factor is niiti. In other words, the function of niiti is to help dharma, to help dharmácarańa [practice of dharma]. Therefore niiti plays a vital role in the life of a sádhaka. But niiti is not the culminating point of life, it is simply a starting point. In order to enter a house one has to pass through the gate, and this passing through the gate is niiti. But one has not gotten into the house simply by passing through the gate; to get in, one has to knock on the door. The entering into the house after knocking on the door is dharma sádhaná. Just to be a moralist is not enough, it only provides one with a passport to enter the house. As said above, Ácárańát dharmah [“Dharma is the assemblage of all your conduct”], and the first phase of your conduct is niiti. Therefore those who are bereft of niiti cannot be dharmic, and those who are dharmic cannot go against niiti.

在法性的第一個階段，幫助最大的就是「導向靈性進步的行為」(niiti)。換言之，其功能就在於幫助法性的鍛鍊(dharmácarańa)。因此，它在靈性修持者的生命裡扮演了重要的角色。然而，它並非生命最極致的目標，而只是一個起點。要進入房子必須經過大門，這道門就是導向靈性進步的行為；然而不是經過大門就可以進到房裡，你還必須敲門，而法性修持就是讓你敲了門進到房裡。光只是成為道德之士是不夠的，那不過是一張入門的通行證。正如上面所說，法性是你所有行為的集合(Ácárańát dharmah)，而第一階段的行為就是「導向靈性進步的行為」(niiti)。故缺乏導向靈性進步的行為的人不可能成為法性的奉行者，而法性的奉行者絕不可能違背導向靈性進步的行為。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

The final goal of dharma is Paramátman, so for a dharma sádhaka there can be no other end. Those sádhakas who think that through sádhaná they will acquire occult powers, are wrong. Or, they may attain supernatural powers, but those powers will not help them to attain Paramátman. Those powers will not satisfy human longings, because even those powers are something worldly. That which we call supernatural is not really so, “supernatural” is rather loose terminology; any power or object which has come within the bondages of the world is not supernatural, but natural. Those who think that sitting in sádhaná they can obtain ańimá, laghimá, mahimá, prápti, prakámya, etc. [names of occult powers], are in delusion. They are simply wasting their valuable time. A devoted sádhaka never aspires for these things. Even if Paramátman comes to such a sádhaka and says, “My child, take all these powers,” the sádhaka will reply, “Paramátman, keep those powers for Yourself. I donʼt need them. I want You, and You alone. I long for You and not for Your powers.”

法性最後的目標是至上意識，因此法性的修持者不會有其他的目標。那些以為透過靈性修持可以獲得法力的修行者是錯誤的，或者說，他們也許會得到法力，但那些法力不會幫助他們達到至上意識。那些法力無法滿足人類的渴望，因為那些依然是世俗之物。我們稱之為「超自然」的東西並不真的是「超自然」，這個字眼其實不夠嚴謹，任何在世俗束縛範圍內的力量或事物都是屬於「自然」的， 而不是「超自然」的。那些認為靜坐修持就可以得到神通法力(ańimá, laghimá, mahimá,prápti, prakámya)的人是在妄想。他們不過是在浪費寶貴的時間。虔誠的修行者絕不會渴望這些。縱使至上意識來到他們身邊說：「孩子！將這些神通力量全部拿去吧！」修行者會回答說：「至上意識，請您自己留著吧！我並不需要。我只渴望您，只想要得到您而不是您的神通。」

A mother tries to coax and cajole her crying son, and offers him some toys to divert his attention, so that she can work in the kitchen. The child stops crying and forgets his mother for the time being. But if he is a bit naughty, he will again resume his effort to reach the breast of his mother. He will throw away the toys and cry for Mother only. And the mother ultimately has to come and take the child on her lap. A devoted sádhaka is like this child. He or she will say, “O Father, this world that I see all around is a plethora of toys. This world took its birth at a certain time, so it will also come to an end at some time or other. Now let the word shrii be defined and explained. What is the meaning of the word shrii? It means “attraction” or “charm”. Sha + ra – ii = shrii. Múrdhanya śa is the acoustic root of the static principle, it is the biija mantra of tamoguńa. Now, ra is the acoustic root of energy. Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

And what is the meaning of jiṋánam? It means the subjectivization of external objectivity. When the external objectivity is subjectivized by you, then you have acquired jiṋánam of that entity, of that object. But for this subjectivization there should be three entities – the knowing entity, the subject; the known entity, the object; and the activating faculty that connects subject with object. So for jiṋánam three entities are prerequisites – the knower, the known, and the activating faculty.
何謂「知識」？它意指「外在客體的主體化」。當你將外在客體主體化，即意指你獲得對於該外在客體的知識。但「主體化」意味著有「能知者」──它是主體、「所知者」──它是客體、以及連接主體和客體的「知的行動能力」等三者的存在。因此對於知識而言，此三者是先決條件──能知者、所知者和知的能力。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

There may be a defect in the knower; there may be a defect in the emanation of the known; or there may be a defect in [the] activating faculty, or jiṋána-kriyá. So in the case of this jiṋánam or jiṋána-kriyá, there is every possibility that it will be imperfect due to certain distortions. But what is actual jiṋána? Actual jiṋána means the complete assimilation of external objectivities. It is átmajiṋána, and in this jiṋána there is no scope for distortion, because in the case of átmajiṋána the three entities mentioned above will not remain. The knower and the known are the same entity in the case of átmajiṋánam. When you know that you yourself are the knower, the jiṋátá, and you yourself are the known, there will remain no linking faculty; so all the three entities – the known, the knower and the activating faculty – become one in the case of átmajiṋánam (complete assimilation of external objectivities). But in the case of the other jiṋánam, as already found, there remain three entities. So átmajiṋánam is the only jiṋánam, it is the proper knowledge; it is, in the true sense of the term, jiṋána.

能知者可能存在著缺陷，所知者的展現也可能呈現著缺陷，或者知的能力上也有缺陷。所以，在這種知識的追求上，有可能會因為某種扭曲，而使得所獲得的知識是不完美的。然而什麼是真正的知識？真正的知識意指將外在客體完全地同化，這就是自我了悟的知識(átmajiṋána)，在自我了悟的知識裡，沒有扭曲失真，因為上述的三者已不復存在，其中， 能知者與所知者在自我了悟中是一體的，當你知道你自己是這個「能知者」(jiṋátá)，知道你自己是這個「所知者」，就不存在著連接兩者的能力，所以能知、知、所知這三者，在自我了悟的知識中變成了一體，即外在客體完全地被同化。可是在其他已經發現到的知識裡，都存在著這三者。是故唯有自我了悟的知識是知識，它才是正確的知識，也就是說，它是真正的知識。

Whenever you come in contact with different objects, physical or mental, under the spell of physical pabulum or mental pabulum, those objects have pictorial colours. Those colours may or may not be visible, but the colours are there. Similarly, whenever you come in contact with any thing, or any external object, those objects have their peculiar acoustic waves also, and those acoustic waves may or may not be audible, but those waves are there. Nowwhen a sádhaka, by dint of his sádhaná, establishes mental equilibrium – a mental equipoise – then what happens? The sádhaka remains in this world and does all his or her mundane duties with mundane objectiv[ities], but the sádhakaʼs mind is never assailed by the colours of those entities. Since his or her mind is not affected or assailed by those entities, then we will say that that sádhaka has established himself or herself in vaerágya. Vaerágya does not mean “renunciation”. That is a defective explanation and interpretation of the term vaerágya. You should remain in this world and do your duty with a balanced mind. Now, Bhagaván Krśńa says, “You leave aside all other dharmas.”(2)All other dharmas are vastu dharmas and jaeva dharma. You need not do anything for vastu dharma, because it is automatic. Nor need you do anything for jaeva dharma, because it is automatic. You feel hungry before a meal, so you feel the urge to satisfy your hunger; you feel thirsty before drinking water, and that is why you try to quench your thirst. You need not do anything particularly for that purpose. But for Bhágavata Dharma you have to do. In another discourse, I already explained that there are three essentialities in Bhágavata Dharma – vistára (expansion), rasa (flow), and sevá (service). Everybody wants expansion. Now for this psychic expansion one is to do spiritual sádhaná. It is the speciality of the human mind, and also of all other minds, that it takes the form of its object. 我在別的演講中已解釋過至上法性有三個要素──擴展(vistára)、波流(rasa)和服務(sevá)。每個人都希望擴展。為了心靈的擴展，人必須從事靈性的修持。心靈會取得其目標的形象，這是人類心靈，也是所有其他心靈的特殊之處。如果心靈以至上意識為目標，心靈自然而然會成為祂。了悟至上意識者會成為至上意識本身(Brahmavid Brahmaevabhavati)。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

The second essentiality is rasa. Rasa means “flow”. You know, whether there is any expression or not, in the Cosmic Citishakti there is a never-ending flow. That flow has no curvature. It moves on just like a straight line. This Citishakti is known as Shiva, also. (When the Citishakti is the Transcendental Entity, Its activating power is Its innate principle. Now when the innate principle or binding principle or activating principle gets the chance to create something concrete, then the Citishakti is known as Shiva. When within the transcendental scope of the Citishakti the activating force does not get the scope to create something concrete, in that case the Citishakti is known as Parashiva, and the nucleus of this Parashiva is known as Ádishiva. For Shiva the English term will be the “Attributed Consciousness”, for Parashiva the “Non-Attributed Consciousness”, and for Ádishiva the “Supreme Noumenal Subjectivity”.) Now in the case of Shiva, that is, in the case of this expressed universe, there is force, there is wave, but those waves are not straight waves. They are not straight lines. There are curvatures in those waves due to the influence of the binding principles of Mahámáyá [the Supreme Operative Principle]. But in the case of Parashiva, the movement is there, but it is in a straight line. So wherever there is Shiva, wherever there is the Cognitive Faculty, wherever there is Citishakti, there must be flow, there must be rasa. That is why it has been said for Him that He is sarvadyotanátmaka akhańd́a cidaekarasah – an “all-vibrating, unbroken flow of cognition”.

其次是「波流」。Rasa意指「波流」。你知道，至上認知力(Citishakti)是一股永無止境的波流，不管有否展現，此一波流沒有曲度，而是像直線般筆直進行。至上認知力又稱為希瓦(Shiva，俱屬性至上本體)。[當至上認知力是超覺的本體時，其作用之力量是屬於它固有之法則；當此固有之法則、束縛法則或作用之法則有機會創造出具體之物時，此至上認知力就稱為希瓦。]當至上認知力處在其超覺之狀態時，其固有之作用力量沒有機會創造具體之物，此時的至上認知力稱為「無上希瓦」(Parashiva，無屬性至上本體)，此無上希瓦的核心就稱為「第一希瓦」(Ádishiva)。「希瓦」以英文來說就是「俱屬性至上意識」；「無上希瓦」就是「無屬性至上意識」；而「第一希瓦」就是「至上主體」。在俱屬性至上意識(Shiva)的情況下，亦即在這個展現的世界裡，存在著力量、波流，但這些波流不是直線波流，因為受到至上運作法則束縛力量所致，它們是有曲度的波流。然而就「無屬性至上意識」(Parashiva)的情況而言，它仍存在著行動，只是它是直線進行的行動。所以，只要有俱屬性至上意識，有至上認知能力之處，就一定會有波流存在。這就是為什麼我們會說祂充滿了波動，是一股永不間斷的認知波流(sarvadyotanátmaka akhańd́a cidaekarasah)之緣故。

The third factor of Bhágavata Dharma is sevá. You know that there are two words, sevá and vyavasáya. The meaning of vyavasáya is “business”. Business is always mutual. If you want one kilo of sugar you will have to pay for it: you give something and they will give you sugar. So business is mutual, not unilateral. But sevá [service] is always unilateral; you give something in sevá but take nothing in return. This is sevá. In the advertisements of certain business concerns, you can find written: “We have been serving the nation for fifty years.” No, no, that is not sevá, it is vyavasáya, because they are being paid for it. The railways are not rendering service to you, because you are paying for your journey by train. If it were unilateral, then only could you have accepted it as service. Another meaning of krśńa is [krśibhuh]. It means “I exist because He exists.” So He is called Krśńasvarúpa. A fish exists because water exists. In that sense, water is krśńa for a fish. Why does a fish exist? Because water exists. Similarly, all living beings exist because He exists. That is why He is Paramasvarúpa for all. This is the real meaning of the word Krśńa. He says: “You leave all other dharmas, give up all other isms, you just follow me, you just follow Bhágavata Dharma, because you are a human being.” Lord Krśńa again says, “Suppose you are a sinner, you are a degraded person, your past was black; even then, if you follow Me, I will liberate you from all the fetters of all sins – all the reactive momenta. I am with you, I am to help you, I am to liberate you.”

Krśńa另一個意義是「krśibhuh」，它的意思是「祂存在，所以我存在」，因此，祂被稱為Krśńasvarúpa。因為水存在，所以魚存在。以這例子而言，水就是魚的克里斯那。為什麼魚可以存在，因為有水之故。同樣的，萬有之所以存在乃因有祂存在。所以祂是萬有一切的至上化身(Paramasvarúpa)。這是Krśńa這個字真正的意義。祂說：「你們將其他所有的法性拋棄，丟掉所有的主義、信仰，只要跟隨著我，跟隨著至上法性，因為你們是人。」上主克里斯那又說：「即使你是個罪人，是墮落的人，你的過去一片黑暗，只要你跟隨著我，我將使你從所有罪業束縛當中解脫出來。我與你同在，我是來幫助你的，是來讓你解脫的。」

You know, sinners are of different standards. A pickpocket and a murderer are not of the same standard. Sinners belong to different standards. Now sudurácára means “the worst sinner”; such a person is even hated by other sinners – is the sinner of sinners. Yet, “If even a sudurácára takes the shelter of Parama Puruśa” – bhajate mámananyábhák – “ensconces himself or herself in Me, surrenders at My altar” – “then that person also will be freed from the bondage of sin” – soʼpi pápavinirmuktah. He or she will definitely be freed from the reactive momenta of all sins. “He or she will be freed from all the bondages of bhava”(3)– mucyate bhavabandhanát. Then that person will become one with Me, will be in Me. A devotee must remember that for him or her, there is only one dharma, and that is Bhágavata Dharma. Through this dharma he or she is taking the shelter of Parama Puruśa. In the past, it may be that that person was a sinner or may be that that person was very good; but that question does not arise here; that person is to take shelter in Parama Puruśa. So a devotee has no other dharma but to take shelter in Him.

你知道， 罪人也有不同等級， 扒手和殺人犯是不同等級。Sudurácára指的是最壞的罪人，連其他的壞人都討厭他，他是罪人之中的罪人。然而，「即使是最壞的罪人來到至上意識的庇護下，若他能將自身安住於我，向我誠服(bhajate mámananyábhák)，那麼我也會讓他從所有的罪業束縛中解脫出來(so’pi pápavinirmuktah)。他一定能夠擺脫所有的罪業， 從業力之洋所有的束縛中獲得自由(mucyatebhavabandhanát)。該人將與我合而為一，將回歸於我。」虔誠者一定要牢記在心，人只有一個法性，那就是至上法性。他將透過至上法性取得至上意識的庇護。一個人可能曾經是罪人，可能曾經是善人，但在這裡都不是問題，而是他要來到至上意識的庇護下。所以，虔誠者沒有其他法性，他唯一的法性就是以祂為庇護。

One of the names ofParama Puruśais “Áshutośa”.Áshumeans “quickly, easily”, soáshutośameans one who can be satisfied quickly and easily. Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

The aim of human life is to attain Parama Puruśa – no other goal can be accepted. But human beings live in a relative world. They have to remain within the spatial, temporal, and personal boundaries. Hence one has to pass oneʼs life maintaining proper adjustment with time, space and person. The goal of human beings is Parama Puruśa–He is the Supreme Entity–the absolute entity. When human beings move towards the absolute world from the relative world they have to maintain proper adjustment with everything. This very adjustment, this very balance, brings about benediction to the society. And the individual entity is also benefited. If someone does not maintain adjustment, the society is not benefited, nor is anyone individually. Due to the absence of balance, oneʼs individual spiritual practice is also disturbed. As a result, oneʼs individual progress is hampered. Not only this, retardation starts taking place. Oneʼs aim should be a proper, well-balanced, continuous journey. One has to move towards Parama Puruśa. Human beings are travellers on the path of eternity, marching ahead without stopping anywhere is their characteristic. They must not stop under any circumstance. The greatest shelter of human beings is Parama Puruśa. Hence they have to move ahead fearlessly. They must be fearless because the most powerful entity of the world is with them. There is no cause for fear, there is no cause for timidity. Whom should one fear if the supreme power is with one? Why should one fear? But one has to move ahead in a balanced way.

人類生命的目標是獲得至上意識—其他的目標都不能當作是生命的目標。但是因為他們活在一個相對的世界裡，只好被侷限在時、空、人物的束縛中。因此，人在生命的過程中必須與時、空、人物等因素做適當的調適。人類的目標是至上意識—祂是至上的本體—是絕對的存在實體。當人從相對的世界朝向絕對的世界前進時，他們必須與所有的事物維持適當的調適。這種調適、這種平衡為這社會帶來福祉，同時也造福了個人。若有人沒有調適好，不但社會無法受益，對任何個人也沒有好處。由於缺乏良好的調適，失去了平衡，使得個人靈性的鍛鍊也受到阻礙，結果個體靈性的進展也被迫停止了。非僅如此，退轉的力量將取而代之。吾人朝向生命目標的旅程應有正確適當的調適，而且應不偏不倚、持續前進。我們必須向著至上意識前進。我們是永恆道上的旅人，無休止地向前進是我們的特質。在任何情況下，我們都不應停留。至上意識是我們最偉大的庇護，所以我們應一無所懼地向前邁進。人們無需恐懼，因為世界上最偉大的實體與他們同在，故沒有害怕的道理，人實無畏縮膽怯的必要。當至上的力量與他們同在時，他們還需要恐懼誰呢？你有何可怕的呢！但是人必須以平衡的方式前進。

While rendering service to the entire society, you will have to move ahead because on the one hand you will be blessed by society, and on the other you will take inspiration from it enabling you to march ahead with much more speed. You must always bear in mind thatthis created world is created by Parama Puruśa. Thus it is very very dear to Him. When you render service to created beings it is as good as serving Him.Human beings are entities who have rationality and intellect. The extent to which human beings can render service to the world is more than that of any other creature. Hence you will always bear in mind that you are the oldest sons and daughters of Parama Puruśa – His dear sons and dear daughters. Hence your duty is to utilize totally and properly this physical body and mind. By thinking always of Him and talking of Him psychic elevation takes place. Go on moving towards Him. In Him alone lies Your individual good and social good. You have come with human body, human intellect. Your human life will become fruitful. By His grace you have a human body and human mind and you should also bear in mind that by His grace alone you have to move ahead in life. By His grace alone He is to be attained. You will attain Him – certainly you will attain Him.

當你為這社會整體服務的同時，你也要記得必須向祂前進。一方面你因服務社會而受到社會對你的祝福回饋；另一方面，你從服務社會當中獲得激勵的力量，讓你能更加速向祂前進。你當永遠牢記於心：這世界是至上意識的創造，所以對祂而言，這世界是非常親愛的，當你對造化之萬有服務時，也等同於對祂從事服務。人類是擁有理性和智力的實體，人類能對世界所做的服務遠甚於其他生物，所以，你們心裡千萬不要忘了，你們是至上意識的最年長的兒女，是祂最親愛的孩子。因此，要好好地善用你們的身體和心靈，將它們的功用發揮至極，是你們的責任。藉著持念祂、談論祂，你們的心靈必然獲得提升。繼續朝向祂前進吧！你個人最大的福祉、社會整體最大的福祉唯有存在於祂。你們業已獲得人身、人的智力來到這個世界，而你們身為人類的生命即將開花結果。在祂的恩典下，你們有了人的身體和人的心靈，也要記得，唯有祂的恩典，你才能在生命中前進，因為有祂的恩典，你才能得到祂。你們必然會得到祂，這是勿庸置疑的。

I have been saying for a long time that human society is a singular entity, that human society is indivisible. People tend to classify human beings as rich or poor, educated or uneducated, etc. Those who are rich today may become poor tomorrow and conversely, those who are poor today may become rich tomorrow. Next comes the question of language. Language is only a vehicle of expression. How does it occur? There are six stages to the expression of language:pará,pashyantii,madhyá,dyotamáná,vaekhariiandshrutigocará.Pará shakti, the seed of all expression, lies in themuládhára cakra, but the seed is not transformed into language. It is just the seed of the idea. This is calledparáin Saḿskrta.Pashyantii, the stage where the seed of the idea sprouts, lies in the next highercakra, that is thesvádiśt́hána. In the next stage,madhyámá, the idea is consolidated to give a picture to it. That is to say, people visualise the form of the idea they want to convey. In themańipura cakrathere is an urge to transform the idea into sound form. In Bengali we sometime say that such and such word is in my mind but I cannot articulate it. That is, the flow of the expression has reachedmańipura cakrabut it is not transmitted through spoken words. The memory, due to distortion, has become a little old so the picture of the word is hazy. Thatʼs why it is difficult to transform the idea into language. In the next stage, that isdyotamáná, the idea acquires the form of language [anáhata cakra].Dyotamánámeans vibrational. In this stage there is some vibrational expression but the exact word is not formed. In the fifth stage, when the vibration reaches the vocal cord, the idea gets transformed into language. This isvaekharii shaktior the transformation of ideas into language. The last stage is calledshrutigocaráand occurs when the word gets vocalized with the help of the tongue. These are the six main stages of the expression of language. In all languagespará,pashyantii,madhyá,dyotamánáare uniform. Only in the fifth and sixth stages is the expression different.

再來我們說到語言。語言只是一種表達的工具。它如何產生的呢？語言的表達有六個階段：Pará、Pashyantii、Madhyámá、Dyotamáná、Vaekharii和Shrutigocará。表達的種子是Pará這個力量，位於海底輪(Muladhara)，但此種子尚未被轉化成語言。它僅僅只是觀念蟄伏的種子，梵文稱為Pará。其後Pashyantii是觀念種子開始萌芽的階段，它位於生殖輪(Svadiśthána)。再下一個階段是Madhyámá，觀念開始具體形成一個意象，意即人們把想說的話形象化。在臍輪(Mańipura)產生一種把觀念轉化為音聲的渴望。有時候我們會說我心中想說某某字，但卻難以清楚的表達出來。這就是說表達之波流已來到臍輪，但尚未透過語言被傳達出來。記憶因受扭曲之故而變得有些老化，所以其字的意象也變得模糊不清，所以不容易將其觀念轉化為語言。第四個階段是Dyotamáná，即觀念取得語言的形式。Dyotamáná意指波動的，在此階段存在著某波動性的表達，但精確的字眼尚未形成。在第五階段當波動來到聲帶時，觀念即轉化為語言，此稱為Vaekharii力量或觀念轉化成為語言。最後一個階段是Shrutigocará，即話語在舌頭的幫助下發出聲音。上述六個階段是語言表達的六個主要過程。在所有的語言中，前四階段都是一樣的，只有在第五和第六個階段有不同的表達。

Due to psychic dilation the crude mind grows still subtler. This increase in subtlety develops in the unit citta the capacity to realize its subjectivity. The subtler is the stage of animation in the process of pratisaiṋcara, the more developed is its ego, and later on it can feel and determine the trend of all its movements. It is at this stage that the evolved unit mind develops within itself both ego and will and can use the momentum (saḿvega) acquired during its previous movement in any direction according to its desire. Before this development of will and ego, expression of the self in a constructive line is not possible. Hence in plant and animal life, where mind is underdeveloped, the vital energy as well as the mind are guided and controlled by the will of the Supreme Mind – the Great Ego. These underdeveloped plants and creatures can have definite progress in the course of pratisaiṋcara, because they are being controlled by the will of the Supreme Ego. By the guidance of Vidyámáyá such a unit mind constantly rises higher and higher, but once will is developed within its scope of activities and a special momentum is acquired, the unit mind can choose any direction according to its desire, that is, it may adopt a course of negative pratisaiṋcara. This stage of mental evolution, when the developed ego decides the direction and can move even towards jad́a (negative pratisaiṋcara) is called the “human being”, or mánuśa, because the entity develops a feeling that it has a mind and a mental force which it can utilize to serve its purpose.

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

It is not that a human has the chance of negative pratisaiṋcara only, due to his or her evolved ego; this ego renders a positive help in the movement towards Puruśottama. In the animate phase the imagination of many works in harmony with the Supreme One. So if the unit mind at that stage of evolution directs its potentialities towards longing for the Great, the unit mind can accelerate its progress (that is, movement towards Puruśottama), and its progress can be many times speedier than what it was at the stages where the citta, being in the crudest form, had not developed self-will but had to move according to the desire of the Macrocosm. In this march towards the supramundane, the unit mind gradually feels a closer touch of Puruśottama, and as the proximity of the two increases, the psychic gap between the reflected consciousness and the reflecting plate goes on diminishing and finally these two merge together. This supreme union of Puruśottama and the unit mind is known as yoga: Saḿyogo yogo ityukto jiivátmá Paramátmanah.

人並非只有反宇宙向心運動的機會，由於具有已開展的自我，使其能在朝向核心意識的運動上有正面幫助。在有生命的階段裏，眾生與至上的想像和諧地運作著。如果個體心靈在此演化的階段將其潛能導向渴望至上，則能加速朝向核心意識的速度。此進步的速度，比起尚未發展出自我感，必須依照大宇宙心靈意志前進的最粗鈍心靈質，甚至快上好幾倍。在朝著超世俗的前進過程中，個體心靈逐漸感受到與核心意識愈來愈親密的接觸，由於兩者愈來愈接近，使反映板與反射意識兩者心理的間隙逐漸消失，並在最後融合為一。此等核心意識與個體心靈的至高融合就稱為「瑜伽」(yoga)：「瑜伽乃個體意識與至上意識融合為一。」(Sam'yoga yogo ityukto jiiva'tma' Parama'tmanah)。

According to the urge of pratisaiṋcara the unit mind goes on dilating because of the ever-increasing reflected density of the Macrocosmic Nucleus. Here the microcosm acts as a mirror and the reflected consciousness is just like the reflection of the rays of the sun, in that, while being reflected, He also associates Himself with the plate. The association inculcates the sameness of the quality and so the associative reflection of the Nucleus – Puruśottama – will develop in the unit mind the broadness of His Cosmic Self and the final culmination of the march of this unitary self, or microcosm. 由於宇宙向心運動的影響，個體心靈因為大宇宙核心的反映密度增加而持續地擴張。在此，個體小宇宙如同鏡子，而反映出的意識恰如陽光的反射，當祂被反映時，也將其自身與反映板連結。此種連結將使兩者愈來愈一致，所以與核心意識的連結會在個體心靈中產生宇宙大我的無限性，同時幫助單一自我或個體小宇宙達成前進之目的。個體及宇宙心靈的齊一性建立之後，此種連結的結果會導致個體小宇宙融入大宇宙心靈中。這就是所謂的「自在解脫」(mukti)。

Thus if the finite subjectivity (unit mind) dwells on the infinite one as its objectivity, it results in the gradual expansion of its self and this enlarged mind finally merges with Puruśottama. Hence such a stage is nothing but mental liberation. Here one of our psycho-philosophic theories works – “Oneness in objectivity results in oneness in subjectivity.” So when the objectivity of the microcosm gets converted into objectivity of the Macrocosm, the jiivátman – the subjective counterpart of the microcosm – is transformed into the subjective counterpart of the Macrocosm, that is, Puruśottama.
所以，如果有限的主體(個體心靈)專注於無限中並以其為目標，將使得小我逐漸擴張，最後此擴展的心靈與核心意識融合。所以此階段只是心靈的解脫而已。阿南達瑪迦的心理-哲學理論適用於此：「與目標的合一導致與宇宙主體的合一。」所以當個體小宇宙的目標轉換成大宇宙心靈時，則個體小宇宙對應主體「個體意識」(jiivat'man)就轉換成大宇宙心靈的對應主體，亦即「核心意識」(Purus'ottama)。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

Not only are the superstitions discarded, but the fundamental principles of some of the existing laws of society, like allegiance to the laws of society and state, take second place. Of primary importance is oneʼs allegiance to Brahma. Harsh social punishment such as creating outcasts or placing restrictions on widows or women in general in participating in certain social functions, do not find any place in our society. Ananda Marga has formed a society which frames its laws on the basis of common ideals in order to develop the idea of the oneness of all humanity. This society is radically different from any existing society, for it provides a society with a common bond where there is no distinction between class or sex, where no one is declared an outcast or punished without being given the chance for self-reform, and where no laws are framed keeping in view the interests of only a few individuals. In such a society no one is weak or downtrodden and no one is allowed to exploit others. Such a society had been dreamed of and advocated earlier by moralists and idealists, but never before has such a system been achieved, as it has been with Ananda Marga, which combines all the qualities of the different economic classes of the world in one individual. Never has such a system been conceived of by any of the numerous thinkers and lawgivers of the world.

不僅要摒除迷信，現今社會的一些基本原則也要丟棄，諸如對國家與社會法律的忠誠等等。對於至上意識的忠誠方為最重要。嚴苛的社會懲罰，像是將人們逐出社會或限制寡婦及一般婦女參與某些社會活動等，在我們的社會是無法立足的。阿南達瑪迦所組成的社會法律乃建立在共同的理想上，以發展「所有人類為一體」的理念。這樣的社會在根本上有異於任何其他現存的社會，因為它提供了一種共通的連繫，沒有階級或性別的歧視，沒有人被逐出社會，沒有人會在未被給予自新的機會前就遭受處罰，而且也沒有任何法律是為了少數個人的利益而制定的。在此種社會裡，沒有人是弱勢或被踐踏的，也沒有人被允許剝削別人。這是一個以前的道德家與理想家所夢寐以求的社會，但卻從未達成像阿南達瑪迦一樣的制度，它將全世界不同經濟等級的所有特質都融合為一。全世界無數的思想家與立法者當中，沒有人曾經構想過此種制度。

Rádhá(1)attained Krśńa through madhura bháva [sweet devotion]. In Krśńa she found everything that was charming and sweet in life. And similarly, when the human mind is influenced by vidyá shakti [introversial force], what happens? All of a sudden it feels that “I should do something. I have a human structure. I am a human being. I should do something. I should act like a human being. I should try to goad myself to the realm of divinity, it is my dharma. His supreme flute. That supreme flute is Krśńa. He creates universal acoustic waves, and those waves bring people towards Him; that is why He is called Krśńa. He is unimaginable, for He is beyond the sphere of imagination. Yes, it is, but these countless forms of this observable world are but His psychic manifestations. Only unit entities are evolved in the sphere of His mind as the objects of the unit minds, whereas countless and endless, big and small, unit entities are being created and recreated in the imagination of Brahma, the possessor of the infinite mind. Apparently they are His “form” in this observable world. But none of these forms of His psychic flow – none of these bubbles that are originating, rising and bursting are the ultimate entities. They are all progressing through spatial, temporal and personal changes with a view to merging in that Supreme Bearing, the Nucleus of the Thought Cycle. That is why we none of these mundane manifestations of Brahma can be taken as permanent and held on to its as such. No matter how charming or captivating a form of His may be, one day it must take its leave from us, must disappear to some unseeable region in response to the beckoning call of time, leaving us behind to rue and wail in profuse tears. Similarly, in the second phase, the done “I”, the objectivated “I” [feelings] of the mind, are withdrawn from that realm of affairs and established in the pure doer “I” feeling. Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

Then, Smara nityamanityatám. Nityam means “always” – “Remember always the transitory nature of things.” [Anityatám means “the ephemeral”, “the transitory”.] That which was in the past, is in the present and will continue to be in the future is nitya. If even one of these three aspects of time be absent, the thing is not nitya. For example, that which is in the present and will continue to be in the future, but was not in the past, is not nitya, but anitya. From among beginning, middle and end, if even one is not there, then that is not nitya. A thing which was born will die one day; that which is unborn will not die. That which comes within the scope of the spatial, temporal and personal factors will alone be born and die, but that which is beyond these three and is the base of them all will neither be born nor die. And that alone is nitya.

最後談到「Smara nityamanityatám」。Nityam意指「永遠」—永遠要記得無常是事物的本質。Anityatám意指「短暫的」。Nitya是指「永恆的」—過去、現在、未來都存在的，缺少其中任何一種，就不是永恆的(nitya)。例如，現在、未來都存在，但過去並不存在的，就不是nitya，而是anitya。少了開始、中間和結束的任何一個部分，就不是nitya。誕生來到這世上的事物終有一天會死亡，沒有出生就不會有死亡。只有來到時、空、人物因素範疇內的事物才會有出生和死亡，超越這些因素之外，就不會有生與死的問題，唯有這樣才是永恆的(nitya)。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

Niiti has a very close association with dharma. What is dharma? That which sustains the jiiva is dharma. And the practical side of dharma is expressed in the words Ácárańát dharmah, that is, “Dharma is the assemblage of all your conduct” – the way you eat, the way you speak, the way you perform sádhaná. If your conduct is good, dharma is with you; if your conduct is not good, dharma is not with you. And if dharma is not with you, what comes about is your sarvanásha, or sarvátmaka vinásha – that is, your physical, mental, and spiritual ruin. Now you may say that your átman cannot be ruined. That is correct, but your átman will not remain in the form of átman. It will become crudified.

道德和法性有著密切的關係。何謂「法性」？維持個體生命的就是法性。其實際的表現在於Ácárańát dharmah這個詞上，它的意思是「法性是你所有行為的集合」—你吃東西的方式、你說話的方式、你從事靈性修持的方式等。如果你的行為是好的，法性即與你同在；如果你的行為是不好的，法性就不與你同行。如果法性不與你同行，就會導致滅絕的後果(sarvanásha或sarvátmaka vinásha)，亦即導致你身、心、靈全面的滅絕。或許你會說靈魂是永遠不滅的，這話誠然沒錯，但你的靈魂不會維持原本靈魂的形態，它會變得粗鈍化。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

In the first stage of dharma, the greatest helping factor is niiti. In other words, the function of niiti is to help dharma, to help dharmácarańa [practice of dharma]. Therefore niiti plays a vital role in the life of a sádhaka. But niiti is not the culminating point of life, it is simply a starting point. In order to enter a house one has to pass through the gate, and this passing through the gate is niiti. But one has not gotten into the house simply by passing through the gate; to get in, one has to knock on the door. The entering into the house after knocking on the door is dharma sádhaná. Just to be a moralist is not enough, it only provides one with a passport to enter the house. As said above, Ácárańát dharmah [“Dharma is the assemblage of all your conduct”], and the first phase of your conduct is niiti. Therefore those who are bereft of niiti cannot be dharmic, and those who are dharmic cannot go against niiti.

在法性的第一個階段，幫助最大的就是「道德」(niiti)。換言之，道德的功能就在於幫助法性的鍛鍊(dharmácarańa)。因此，它在靈性修持者的生命裡扮演了重要的角色。然而，它並非生命最極致的目標，而只是一個起點。要進入房子必須經過大門，這道門就是道德；然而不是經過大門就可以進到房裡，你還必須敲門，而法性修持就是讓你敲了門進到房裡。光只是成為道德之士是不夠的，那不過是一張入門的通行證。正如上面所說，法性是你所有行為的集合(Ácárańát dharmah)，而第一階段的行為就是「道德」(niiti)。故缺乏道德的人不可能成為法性的奉行者，而法性的奉行者絕不可能違背道德。

Now the question crops up whether niiti is a relative factor or an absolute factor. Niiti is not cent percent relative, but it is not absolute, either, because niiti does not have any direct relation with Paramátman – it cannot by its own force help one attain Him. 現在問題是「道德」是相對的還是絕對的要素。「道德」不是百分之百相對的，但也不是絕對的，因為它和至上意識並無直接關聯—人無法靠著道德力量而達到至上意識。「道德」是相對世界與絕對世界一種和諧的混合。

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

The final goal of dharma is Paramátman, so for a dharma sádhaka there can be no other end. Those sádhakas who think that through sádhaná they will acquire occult powers, are wrong. Or, they may attain supernatural powers, but those powers will not help them to attain Paramátman. Those powers will not satisfy human longings, because even those powers are something worldly. That which we call supernatural is not really so, “supernatural” is rather loose terminology; any power or object which has come within the bondages of the world is not supernatural, but natural. Those who think that sitting in sádhaná they can obtain ańimá, laghimá, mahimá, prápti, prakámya, etc. [names of occult powers], are in delusion. They are simply wasting their valuable time. A devoted sádhaka never aspires for these things. Even if Paramátman comes to such a sádhaka and says, “My child, take all these powers,” the sádhaka will reply, “Paramátman, keep those powers for Yourself. I donʼt need them. I want You, and You alone. I long for You and not for Your powers.”

法性最後的目標是至上意識，因此法性的修持者不會有其他的目標。那些以為透過靈性修持可以獲得法力的修行者是錯誤的，或者可以這麼說，他們或許會得到法力，但那些法力不會幫助他們達到至上意識。那些法力無法滿足人類的渴望，因為那些依然是世俗之物。我們稱之為「超自然」的東西並不真的是「超自然」，這個字眼其實不夠嚴謹，任何在世俗束縛範圍內的力量或事物都是屬於「自然」的，而不是「超自然」的。那些認為靜坐修持就可以得到神通法力(ańimá, laghimá, mahimá, prápti, prakámya)的人錯了。他們不過是在浪費寶貴的時間。虔誠的修行者從來不會想要這些東西。縱使至上意識來到他們身邊說：「孩子！將這些神通力量全部拿去吧！」修行者也會拒絕：「至上意識，請您自己留著吧！我並不需要。我只渴望您，只想要得到您而不是您的神通。」

Translate the following discourse excerpt into Traditional Chinese:

A mother tries to coax and cajole her crying son, and offers him some toys to divert his attention, so that she can work in the kitchen. The child stops crying and forgets his mother for the time being. But if he is a bit naughty, he will again resume his effort to reach the breast of his mother. He will throw away the toys and cry for Mother only. And the mother ultimately has to come and take the child on her lap. A devoted sádhaka is like this child. He or she will say, “O Father, this world that I see all around is a plethora of toys. This world took its birth at a certain time, so it will also come to an end at some time or other. This world has not been given permanently to anybody.” If God is asked whether He has given this world-toy to anybody forever, He will not be able to answer, for He does not give things forever. He gives with the right hand and takes away with the left.

一位母親試圖哄她哭泣的孩子，拿了一些玩具來轉移孩子的注意力，讓自己可以繼續在廚房做事。孩子有了玩具暫時忘了母親不再哭泣，但是如果孩子不從，非要喝奶不可，他就會丟掉玩具，一直哭著要母親。母親沒有辦法，最後只好來到他身邊將他抱起。虔誠的修行者就像這個小孩，他會說：「哦！至上的父親！這世界的一切都是玩具，既然它在某個時間點誕生，也必會在某個時間點結束，它不是永恆的。」如果有人問上主祂是不是將此一玩具世界永遠地賜予人類，祂是無法回答的，因為祂並沒有賜予任何永恆之物，而是以右手給予又以左手收回。

所以我們知道甚至於經典裡都有這麼多不同的意見—shrutayo vibhinnáh—經典眾說紛紜。而在smrtis裡也都不同。什麼是smrti？smrti意指「個人世俗生活的規範」；「個人靈性生活的規範」稱為「經典」(shruti)，經典就是靈性法典(dharmashástra)，而「個人世俗生活的規範」(smrti)就是「社會法典」(samájashástra)。在古時候，有「帕拉沙瓦法典」(Parashar Saḿhitá)、「那拉達法典」( Nárada Saḿhitá)、「摩奴法典」(Manu Saḿhitá)；而在今日有「印度教法典」(Hindu Code)。這些全部都是社會法典。社會法典的相對性比經典更甚，因為社會會隨著時間而變化。但是經典也一樣彼此之間有許多差異，同時每個聖人(muni)所言也都各不相同(Naekamuniryasya mataḿ nabhinnam)，有些聖人說要以這種方式獻祭，有些則說要以別種方式。而事實上，這些人之中又不是全都是真正覺悟的聖者。唯有「心靈已融入至上意識者」才是真正覺悟的聖者(muni)—Munih dugdhabálakah munih saḿliinamánasah。
